title: fix(update): bind the Windows candidate executor by its handoff identity instead of process ancestry
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Windows update candidates can fail with `Candidate executor binding does not match its parent` even when the recorded update owner and candidate lease are current, because admission additionally requires the candidate's immediate parent PID to equal the recorded spawner.

Refs #166004. Thanks to @wqj11a for the independent reproduction and lease observations, and @H0Nm4M1suZu for the original report.

## User Impact

A Windows candidate can continue an authorized handoff when its launcher ancestry differs from the recorded spawner. The candidate-side repair accepts existing handoff formats from older installed updaters without new options or schema changes. It does not repair the separate plugin-migration/readiness and Scheduled Task recovery symptoms in the issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing candidate binding and delegated executor owners now use the lease store's live executor-ownership check on Windows. The security property remains: only the PID/start identity registered for this run and installation may perform effects while the exact lease generation, original owner, and spawner remain current. Foreign PIDs, changed start identities, and revoked owners are refused. The existing fallback for an unreadable self identity still requires the immediate live parent; POSIX ancestry checks remain unchanged. Windows creation times retain their existing millisecond normalization and exact comparison.

The related report #166509 needs a separate finalization/recovery repair. Package rollback already restores Scheduled Task autostart before restarting the verified previous package. In the already-current flow, however, fresh Doctor can park the Gateway into `rollbackStopState` while error recovery still receives `params.preManagedServiceStop`; that older receipt may say `stopped: false`. The redacted report does not establish its exact refusal or whether state remained restart-compatible. This PR does not claim to fix it.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the extended Windows fixture produced two failures at the exact reported binding error; seven other identity cases passed. Afterward, all 42 executor tests passed in three runs of `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/update-command-executor.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 33.50 s, 40.30 s, and 48.96 s wall time, including shared preparation. Measured test time was 13.740 s, 15.387 s, and 27.124 s; no individual test exceeded 5.9 s.
- The existing fixture exercises real lease admission and nested delegation with Windows process facts. Controls cover foreign PIDs, mismatched start identities, missing identity without a direct parent, and revocation before effects.
- One importer invocation selected 76 direct/barrel callers. The default runner executed 75 files: 73 passed, one was platform-skipped, and `src/infra/update-repair-agent.e2e.test.ts` failed two existing per-turn-budget cases. The remaining Node-provisioning live file was explicitly routed through the live config and skipped by its existing opt-in guard (one test). Passed groups: unit 11, tooling 19, infrastructure 627, config I/O 113, CLI process 126, CLI 426, commands 10, E2E 10 tests. There were 26 existing platform/runtime skips. Total invocation wall time was 2,509.66 s, including an 8m 50.3s E2E prerequisite build.
- The two repair E2E failures were `preserves released behavior and scopes repair inference (turn, validating)` (68.358 s) and `(turn, verifying)` (72.338 s). Diagnostics attribute 61.591 s across 103 checks and 63.569 s across 81 checks to synchronous requester/run-state authority reads. Executor fencing used only 63 ms / 50 ms. The unchanged `update-repair-turn-worker.ts` calls both readers inside each authority check; these repeatedly create read-only SQLite snapshots. This Windows-specific change retains the same admission path on this macOS run. No baseline replay was run, and no passing replay is claimed. This needs separate repair-authority/state-snapshot performance work; timeouts, assertions, and production authority checks were not relaxed. These failures remain open as a separate performance follow-up; the importer validation is not fully green.
- Other existing slow cases: database rollback `convergence` 48.162 s; fleet Doctor preflight `reuses the admitted original capture...` 33.372 s; candidate authority `healthy` 36.631 s. These compose real process/state transitions and were left unchanged.
- Published grant compatibility passed for 2026.9.6 numeric/bridge and 2026.9.7 exact identities, including parent replacement refusal.
- P1 Codex autoreview was attempted with isolated review inputs and failed with HTTP 401 (`reviewer_unavailable`, no report). Independent review of the PR head is still outstanding.
- The first changed-file check passed types and preceding guards but caught `no-map-spread` in the added test table. Replaced it with equivalent `Object.assign`; all three final touched-suite repeats passed, and the final `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed (exit 0), including core/test typechecking, lint, and all selected guards. `git diff --check` also passed.
- This is local macOS boundary proof with isolated state, not a native Windows Scheduled Task or published-package upgrade run. Hosted CI timing is not yet available.
- Diff: production +15/-5, tests +44/-19, docs +7/-0. No config, CLI, dependency, or schema changes.
